subject: BrightLane model shortlist, context needs & token risk map
messages:
From: Samir Khatri <samir@brightlane.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: BrightLane — model shortlist & context planning

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the intro last week. We want to get the model selection and usage assumptions locked so your CS/implementation team can hand us off cleanly to Eng. Quick summary of our needs:

- Primary feature: smart contract suggestion + clause highlighting for our SME workflows.
- Typical document sizes: 1–6 pages (most around 3 pages).
- Useful context window: up to 16k tokens for the top 10% of cases, 8k covers ~70% of requests.
- Traffic: ~4,500 active users, ~0.8 interactions/user/day, average 1.6 requests/session.
- Expected avg tokens per request (prompt + response): ~450 tokens.

I attached a small sample of prompts (brightlane_sample_prompts.csv) and a 7‑day snapshot of usage (brightlane_usage_snapshot.xlsx).

Ask: can you share a recommended shortlist (3 tiers) with latency and rough monthly token cost estimates and any recommendations for caching/prefixing? Also let us know if you foresee any material risks with 16k windows.

Thanks — Samir

Attachments: brightlane_sample_prompts.csv (text/csv, 12KB), brightlane_usage_snapshot.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48KB)

Hi Samir,

Appreciate the data — this is perfect for an initial pass. Key clarifying questions before we propose final tiers:

- What percent of requests include attachments (PDFs) that you expect us to encode into the prompt vs. plain text?
- Do you need any hard latency SLO for interactive UIs (e.g., 300ms token latency vs 800ms)?
- For the 16k cases, are those full-document summaries or rare deep dives for a handful of users?

Plan: I’ll prepare a 3‑tier model shortlist with estimated monthly token counts and cost bands; Ben will add latency/cost tradeoffs and Grace will propose a caching/prefix plan to reduce tokens for repeat contexts. We should sync on a 30‑minute tech review — is Thursday 6/15 at 11am PT possible for you?

I’ll share the model shortlist PDF and a mutual action plan after internal alignment.

— Hannah

Ask (short):

- Grace: propose a short caching strategy (prefix cache + user session KV) and an ops-safe fallback policy (if high‑context model unavailable, fallback to 8k model with summarized context).

I attached the usage snapshot again for reference. Will collect your bullets and send to Samir in the afternoon.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khatri <samir@brightlane.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightLane — model shortlist & context planning

Hannah — quick draft below. Numbers are ballpark; I used Samir's 4,500 MAU → ~108k interactions/month and avg 450 tokens/request (~48.6M tokens/mo).

Shortlist (3 tiers):
- Tier A — Cost‑saver (start here if budget‑constrained):
  • Model: Llama2-13B‑q4_8k (8k native window)
  • Performance: good for short prompts, struggles on 16k documents (requires chunk+summary approach)
  • Latency: ~60–90ms/token on a p3-like shape (batching friendly)
  • Estimated monthly cost: ~ $0.012/token equivalent * 48.6M ≈ $583k (note: this is indicative on hosted pricing tiers; exact depends on reserved vs hosted).

- Tier B — Recommended (balance of accuracy, cost, and 16k support):
  • Model: RedMosaic-30B‑16k (quantized q5_0)
  • Performance: supports native 16k, strong on retrieval/summarization tasks
  • Latency: ~90–140ms/token (lower with batching; reserve headroom for SLOs)
  • Estimated monthly cost: ~ $0.018/token * 48.6M ≈ $875k

- Tier C — High accuracy / low-latency priority (for small subset of sessions):
  • Model: RedMosaic-65B‑32k (float16 or advanced quant)
  • Performance: best accuracy on long documents, good for critical-charge cases
  • Latency: ~140–220ms/token (higher infra cost)
  • Estimated monthly cost: ~ $0.035/token * 48.6M ≈ $1.7M

Risk map / notes:
- Token volume dominates cost: reducing avg tokens/request by 25% via prompt engineering or caching cuts costs materially.
- 16k native models increase infra footprint but reduce complexity vs chunk+summary.
- For pilot, recommend Tier B for majority of traffic + Tier A for non‑critical endpoints; selectively route heavy 16k sessions to Tier C for pilot users.

Operational suggestions:
- Use per‑route routing: low‑latency endpoints -> Tier B; background batch jobs -> Tier A (cheaper).
- Implement prefix caching for repeated clauses (Grace to specify).

I can produce a one‑page cost/accuracy chart and a short fallback playbook if useful.

— Ben
